extracted.intended_audience: European patent applicants and practitioners (patent attorneys), especially those who have received an EPO Rule 71(3) communication
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural checklist and requirements for what an applicant must do after receiving an EPO communication under Rule 71(3) indicating intention to grant (checking Druckexemplar, filing amendments or paying fees, translations, validation, and post-grant steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond within 4 months to Rule 71(3) communication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant does not reply to the communication within 4 months, by completing the acts under A or B, the application will be deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 4-month period is strict: take either option A (file amendments) or B (no amendments and pay fees/file translations). Failure to act = deemed withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check the Druckexemplar thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication is accompanied by the version of the application text that the EPO intends to grant, known as the 'Druckexemplar'. The Druckexemplar is taken to be the authentic text of a granted patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Druckexemplar becomes the authentic granted text, carefully verify all claims, description and drawings; note any suggested Examiner amendments intended to correct minor deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: If proposing amendments: state proposed amendments and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant wishes to make amendments to the text of the Druckexemplar, the applicant must respond within the 4-month period, stating the proposed amendments and giving the reasons for the amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Examining Division may issue a second intention to grant including a new Druckexemplar if it has no objections; however the Division can reopen substantive examination if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no amendments: pay grant and printing fees and file claim translations within 4 months
rubrics_metrics.description: If no amendments to the Druckexemplar are necessary, grant and printing fees must be paid within a 4-month period and translations of the claims into the other two official EPO languages must be filed by the same deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims fees may also be due if the number of claims has increased during examination. Ensure correct payments and translations are filed to progress to grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims fees for increased number of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims fees may be due if the number of claims has increased during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check claim count relative to fee schedule and pay any additional claims fees together with grant/printing fees as required within the 4-month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to grant is issued after approval, payment and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: After the applicant has approved the text, paid the fees and filed the claims translations, the EPO issues a 'Decision to grant' notice stating the date on which the patent will be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant is then mentioned in the European Patent Journal on its date of grant; track the Decision to grant and announced date carefully for downstream deadlines (e.g., divisional filing limit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application deadline (parent must be pending)
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application can only be filed whilst the parent is still pending, i.e. up until the day before the date of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File any desired divisionals before the grant date (parent no longer pending on the date of grant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation requirements in designated states (translations/fees/time limits vary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the EPO states in which patent protection is sought, it may be necessary to file translations with national patent offices and/or pay further fees for the patent to take effect in those national states ('validation'). The required acts and time limits vary by state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check national requirements for each desired state carefully and complete translations and national fees within the relevant deadlines; after validation the EP patent effectively becomes a bundle of national rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition window and standing (9 months post-grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 9 months of the date of grant, any third party may file an opposition against the patent with the aim of getting the patent revoked or limited centrally at the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the 9-month opposition period following grant during which third parties can challenge validity centrally at the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The grounds upon which a patent can be opposed are that the subject-matter of the patent is not patentable (e.g., not new or not inventive), that the invention is not disclosed clearly and completely enough for a person skilled in the art to carry it out, and/or that the patent’s subject-matter extends beyond the content of the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents commonly rely on lack of novelty/inventive step, insufficiency of disclosure, or added subject-matter; prepare to defend these specific legal grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition proceedings process and possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings typically involve rounds of submissions by each party, followed by a hearing where an EPO opposition board decides on the outcome. At the end, the patent may be maintained as granted, maintained with amendments or revoked in full; the decision applies to all designated states and can be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions can be lengthy; consider strategic responses, settlement, or appeal options. The centrally-decided outcome affects all national parts of the EP patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: National renewal fees to maintain validated national rights (up to 20 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep the 'bundle' of granted national rights in force in each state in which the patent was validated, annual renewal fees must be paid to the national offices. These amounts vary and typically increase as the patent gets older. A patent can be kept in force up until 20 years from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and pay national renewal fees in each validated state on time; non-payment in a state will lapse protection in that state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement requires national proceedings in each state
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a patent has been granted it can be enforced. As a European patent is effectively a bundle of national rights, any enforcement proceedings must be started separately in each state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan enforcement (litigation/injunctions/damages) on a country-by-country basis according to each state's procedures and remedies.
